summary: The Solar Energy Industries Association and Advanced Energy United protest MISO's LARS filing as unduly discriminatory because only the Associated Transmission Customer, often a vertically integrated utility, can submit an application. They also object to generator stranding risk and LARS and DPP coordination.
ask: Reject LARS with guidance to let any qualified participant apply directly; alternatively accept it and clarify that the application role must be administered without discrimination.

points.point: Only the LARS Associated Transmission Customer, often a load-serving entity, can start an application.
points.quote: The LARS Associated Transmission Customer is the only party that may initiate the LARS Application.

points.point: They say independent producers can join only if the utility competitor lets them, with no duty to submit.
points.quote: Yes, independent power producers can participate in the LARS process

points.point: They ask FERC to reject LARS and direct a refiling that lets any qualified market participant apply directly to MISO.
points.quote: reject the LARS proposal, on the grounds that the proposal is unduly discriminatory

points.point: A generator whose paired load leaves in the first fifteen years can lose its LLGIA and must re-enter the DPP.
points.quote: the generator's LLGIA ultimately will be terminated and the generator must obtain new Interconnection Service through the Definitive Planning Process (DPP) to continue operating.

points.point: MISO offers only a transition period of up to one year, which they contrast with SPP's five-year HILLGA approach.
points.quote: MISO proposes only a temporary transition period of up to one year

points.point: They say LARS studies leave out queued DPP projects without executed GIAs, so the two processes use different assumptions.
points.quote: MISO specifically states that LARS studies will not include interconnection requests currently in the generator interconnection queue that have not executed GIAs.

points.point: In the alternative, they ask FERC to clarify that the Associated Transmission Customer must apply the same standards and timelines it uses for its own projects.
points.quote: the Commission expects the LARS Associated Transmission Customer to apply the same submission standards and timelines it applies to its own similarly situated projects.

throughLine.text: Protests MISO's LARS filing, offered as its answer to the E-8 show cause order on electrically proximate load, as discriminatory in who may apply and uncertain for generators and queued projects.
